text:
The Blues made a change in goal this week, and it was news across the league: Joel Hofer has replaced Jordan Binnington as St. Louis' starter, as ESPN reported on Monday. The numbers had been pointing there for a while. Hofer has saved 11.6 goals more than his shots would predict this season (expected goals measure the quality of each chance), and over his last five starts he is .919 against hard shots. Tonight he faces the hottest goalie in the matchup. Jake Oettinger is .949 over his last five starts, with 8.9 goals saved above expected, and 13.8 for the season.

That is the honest read on both teams' recent runs. Dallas went 4-1-0 in its last five while taking only 44% of the expected goals, and St. Louis has points in five straight (4-0-1) on 46%. Two hot goalies have been covering for a lot. The season-long five-on-five shares are dead even at 50%, and our numbers have it nearly level, 2.78 expected goals for Dallas and 2.75 for St. Louis. The one meeting so far, on Oct. 2, went 4-0 to the Blues in a game they deserved to win only 41% of the time.

Both teams lost Wednesday, Dallas ending a five-game winning streak against Nashville and St. Louis a four-game run in a shootout on Long Island, where it played without Jimmy Snuggerud and Pavel Buchnevich. Both are day-to-day and listed as questionable, and both are in our numbers. Snuggerud has goals in three straight and seven points in five career games against Dallas. Robert Thomas has 11 points in a five-game point streak, and Logan Mailloux, flagged as a breakout, has nine points in eight.

Dallas has its own stories. Jamie Benn reached 1,000 career points earlier this month. Jason Robertson is playing another contract year, his name tied to a reported Kraken offer, and TSN's headline says he is happy with the Stars "right now." Wyatt Johnston brings a six-game point streak (five goals), and we have him at 38% to score.
headline: Joel Hofer's net now, and Oettinger's on fire
